_comment: Raptor's egg library (library/README.md). Written for Raptor.
name: Ergo
author: support@raptorpanel.net
description: Ergo is a modern IRC server with accounts, history and bouncer features built in. The egg runs plain IRC on the server's port, with the other settings in ircd.yaml.
startup: export ERGO__NETWORK__NAME="${NETWORK_NAME}" ERGO__SERVER__NAME="${SERVER_HOSTNAME}"; if [ -n "${OPER_PASSWORD:-}" ]; then export ERGO__OPERS__ADMIN__PASSWORD="$(printf '%s\n' "$OPER_PASSWORD" | ./ergo genpasswd --quiet)"; fi; exec ./ergo run --conf ircd.yaml

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Ergo: downloads the release for the chosen version from GitHub (checked
# against GitHub's checksum) and writes a first ircd.yaml. The settings
# (ircd.yaml), the MOTD and the database (ircd.db: accounts, channels) are
# never touched; the binary is replaced only once the new one has arrived.
set -euo pipefail
cd /mnt/server
work=/mnt/server/.raptor-build
rm -rf "$work" && mkdir -p "$work"
trap 'rm -rf "$work"' EXIT
fail() { echo "$1"; exit 1; }
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64) arch=x86_64 ;;
    aarch64) arch=arm64 ;;
    *) fail "Ergo has no build for this CPU ($(uname -m))." ;;
esac

want="${VERSION:-latest}"
tag=latest
if [ "$want" != latest ]; then tag="v${want#v}"; fi
tag=$(gh-release tag ergochat/ergo "$tag") || fail "Ergo has no version $want. Set Version to latest, or to a release such as 2.19.1, then reinstall."
version="${tag#v}"

if [ -x ergo ] && [ "$(./ergo --version 2>/dev/null)" = "ergo-$version" ]; then
    echo "Ergo $version is already installed."
else
    echo "Downloading Ergo $version"
    gh-release download ergochat/ergo "$tag" "ergo-$version-linux-$arch.tar.gz" "$work/ergo.tar.gz"
    tar -xzf "$work/ergo.tar.gz" -C "$work" --strip-components=1
    rm -rf languages
    mv "$work/languages" languages
    cp -f "$work/default.yaml" default.yaml
    [ -f ircd.motd ] || cp "$work/ergo.motd" ircd.motd
    mv -f "$work/ergo" ergo
fi

# A first configuration from Ergo's own default: plain IRC on the server's
# port (Raptor keeps it there), and the admin operator's example password
# replaced with a random one nobody knows, until Operator password is set.
if [ ! -f ircd.yaml ]; then
    [ -f default.yaml ] || ./ergo defaultconfig > default.yaml
    hash=$(head -c 24 /dev/urandom | base64 | ./ergo genpasswd --quiet)
    awk -v hash="$hash" '
        /^    listeners:/ {
            print
            print "        # Raptor sets the next line to the server'"'"'s port at every start. Add other"
            print "        # listeners with an address, such as \"0.0.0.0:6697\" (TLS) or \"127.0.0.1:6668\"."
            print "        \":6667\": {}"
            skip = 1; next
        }
        skip && /^    [a-z#]/ { skip = 0 }
        skip { next }
        /^opers:/ { opers = 1 }
        opers && /^        password: / { print "        password: \"" hash "\""; opers = 0; next }
        /^motd: |^    motd: / { sub(/ergo\.motd/, "ircd.motd") }
        { print }
    ' default.yaml > ircd.yaml.new
    grep -q '^        ":6667": {}' ircd.yaml.new && grep -qF "$hash" ircd.yaml.new || fail "Ergo's default configuration has changed shape, so ircd.yaml couldn't be written. Report this to Raptor."
    mv ircd.yaml.new ircd.yaml
    echo "Wrote a first ircd.yaml (plain IRC on the server's port)."
fi
echo "Installed Ergo $version."

variables.name: Version
variables.description: The Ergo version to install, such as 2.19.1, or latest. Reinstall to change it.

variables.name: Network name
variables.description: The network's name, shown to people when they connect.

variables.name: Server hostname
variables.description: The server's name on the network, a hostname such as irc.example.com.

variables.name: Operator password
variables.description: The password for the admin operator, used with /OPER admin <password>. No spaces; leave it empty to have no usable operator.
